column1: In an influential article, Bernanke (1983) provided evidence consistent with an important role for nonmonetary financial factors in accounting for the severity of the Great Depression in the United States. After controlling for unexpected money growth, he found that proxies for the financial crises of the early 1930s contributed significantly to explaining the growth rate of industrial production in his regression analysis.40 If pure monetary causes were responsible for the decline in output during the Depression, the other measures of financial disruptions should not add explanatory power to the regression.
